chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Fazalah ibn Ayyub, from the one who mentioned it, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), so an overhang from the overhangs of the mosque fell and struck a man, but it did not harm him, and injured his leg. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Ask him what he did today.' So they asked him, and he said: 'I went out, and in my sleeve was a date. So I passed by a beggar and gave him a date in charity.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'By it, Allah repelled [the harm] from you.'

key_terms.شُرْفَةٌ: An overhang or projecting part of a building
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الرَّسُولِ: The Mosque of the Messenger (Prophet Muhammad)

ai.seo_question: How does charity repel affliction according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) attributes the man's survival from a falling overhang in the Prophet's Mosque to his charity of a single date, illustrating the principle that *sadaqah* (charity) repels divine affliction (*bala'*). This incident highlights the Shia scholarly understanding that even minor acts of charity serve as a spiritual shield, transforming potential major calamities into minor, manageable injuries as an act of divine mercy.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from the one who mentioned it, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I was with Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> in the Masjid of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so an overhang from the overhangs of the Masjid fell off. So it fell upon a man, but it did not harm him, and injured his leg. So, Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ask him which thing he has done today’. So they asked him, and he said, ‘I went out, and in my sleeve was one date. So I passed by a beggar, and I gave in charity to him with a date’. So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By it, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Repelled from you’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from ‘Abd Allah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from those he has mentioned from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I was in the presence of abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in the Masjid of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause. At that time, one of the extended over-hangings of the Masjid fell on a man and injured his leg. Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, told us to ask him about what he has done today. When people asked him about it, he said, ‘When I came out of my home, there were some dates in my sleeve. I passed by a beggar and gave him one piece of date as charity. 5 Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘That is the reason why Allah repelled misfortune from you.”’
